data.narrative:
Epsilon3, a Series A space and aerospace company founded by Laura Crabtree and Max Mednik, has raised $19M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader peer set of 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Stage-progression represents the only reliably applicable method given data constraints. Using $19M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-round progression yields $38M. This method reflects observed market norms for capital deployment and dilution at this stage. Peer-median triangulation was not viable: while 11 same-sector peers exist, only 2 occupy adjacent stages, falling short of the minimum 3 datapoints needed for statistical defensibility. Public-comp anchoring is inapplicable without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies do not typically provide.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M–$44M, with a median of $38M. This relatively tight band reflects reliance on a single methodological pillar. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peer benchmarks, revenue trajectory visibility, and the absence of comparable recent Series A transactions in the space sector. Any valuation outside this range would require either new revenue disclosures or access to recent private-market transaction data in aerospace. Management's ability to deploy the $19M raised will materially affect subsequent funding outcomes.
